title: Add community knowledge: AL boolean operators do not short-circuit
summary: Two community knowledge articles explain AL's lack of short-circuit evaluation for boolean operators and recommend using case statements as alternatives for complex condition chains.
key_points: AL boolean operators (and, or, xor) do not guarantee short-circuit evaluation, meaning all operands are evaluated regardless of the left operand's result
Demonstrates how this can cause silent bugs like accessing uninitialized records or array out-of-bounds conditions
Provides pattern for or conditions using early exit (if A then exit(true); exit(B);) instead of nested if rewrite
Recommends case true/false of statements as flatter alternative for condition chains longer than three nested if statements
Includes good and bad code examples for both boolean operator patterns and case statement usage
quote: AL gives no short-circuit (lazy) evaluation guarantee for `and`, `or`, or `xor`.
